fatal_errors: The proposed ball-milling/SPS route does not reconstruct the target liquid-metal dealloying method: immersion of directionally segregated WTaVTi in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h.
The cited paper concerns an NbMoCrTiAl composite reinforced with TiC and Al2O3 and provides no evidence that ball milling plus SPS enables stable RHEA–Cu composites.
The hypothesis incorrectly treats rapid kinetics as overcoming positive mixing enthalpy; rapid processing does not remove the underlying thermodynamic immiscibility.
The proposed homogeneous dispersion conflicts with the target bicontinuous, directionally aligned RHEA-ligament/Cu-channel architecture and its W-rich passivating interface.

The suggested SPS temperature of approximately 1700 °C places Cu far above its melting point and is transferred from an unrelated Cu-free system without evidence of Cu retention or structural stability.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad RHEA–Cu compatibility problem, but otherwise misses the paper's intervention, conditions, architecture, mechanism, and measured outcomes. The target method is liquid-metal dealloying, in which Cu selectively replaces Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels while W/Ta/V-rich ligaments remain; a roughly 300 nm W-rich interlayer passivates the interface. The generated route instead proposes generic mechanical alloying and SPS based on evidence from a different alloy and reinforcement system containing no Cu. Its comparative experiment could test whether that alternative route improves uniformity, but it does not discriminate the selective-exchange/passivation mechanism or address the target thermal-conductivity and helium-swelling results.
